steps.ask: The test is two-tailed. How does the p-value relate to the area beyond |z| in one tail?
steps.title: Find the two-tailed p-value

lines.text: Round $\hl{1}{|z|}$ to $\hl{1}{1.79}$. The test is two-tailed, so $\hl{3}{p} = 2\left[1 - P(z < \hl{1}{1.79})\right]$.
From the tables, $P(z < \hl{1}{1.79}) = 0.9633$.

steps.ask: Compare the p-value with the 5% significance level. What does that tell you about H₀?
steps.title: Compare with the 5% level and conclude

lines.text: $\hl{3}{0.0734} > \hl{4}{0.05}$, so we do not reject the null hypothesis.
There is not enough evidence to say the news report's claim of 21 hours is incorrect.

problems.final: \hl{3}{p = 0.0734}; \text{ not enough evidence to reject the claim}

problems.note: The test statistic is negative this time, so the tail lies below -1.71 and you start from the lower tail. The doubling rule is the same as problem 1, and the answer is explained in words at the end.

steps.ask: The test is two-tailed and z is negative. Which tail area do you need, and how do you get it from the table?
steps.title: Find the probability in the tail

lines.text: Because the test is two-tailed, $\hl{3}{p}$ is twice the area below $z = \hl{1}{-1.71}$.

steps.ask: One tail gives only half of what a two-tailed test needs. What do you do to the tail area?
steps.title: Double it for both tails

steps.ask: Put the p-value into words: what chance does it describe, and is it small enough to reject H₀ at 5%?
steps.title: Explain what it represents

lines.text: If the true mean spend really were $\text{€}94$, there would be about an 8.72% chance of getting a sample mean at least as far from $\text{€}94$ as $\text{€}90.45$ (that is, $\text{€}90.45$ or less, or $\text{€}97.55$ or more).
Since $\hl{3}{0.0872} > \hl{4}{0.05}$, this is not unusual enough to reject $H_0$.

problems.note: The p-value is given this time, so there is no calculation, only the comparison. It is below 0.05, so H₀ is rejected, the opposite of the first two problems.

steps.ask: The p-value is already given. Is it smaller or larger than the significance level, and what does that mean for H₀?
steps.title: Compare the p-value with the significance level

lines.text: The significance level is 5%, which is $\hl{4}{0.05}$.
The p-value $\hl{3}{0.024}$ is less than $\hl{4}{0.05}$, so we reject the null hypothesis that the average speed is unchanged.

issues: Notes on problems 2 and 3 claimed only the result changed; now mention s vs σ and the new n.

steps.ask: The question asks whether the mean has changed. What do H₀ and H₁ say?
steps.title: State the hypotheses

lines.text: $H_0$: the mean weight of carry-on luggage has not changed ($\mu = \hl{2}{12}$ kg).
$H_1$: the mean weight of carry-on luggage has changed ($\mu \ne \hl{2}{12}$ kg).

steps.ask: Standardise the sample mean against the hypothesised mean, using σ/√n. What goes on top, and what on the bottom?
steps.title: Calculate the test statistic

steps.ask: Compare the test statistic with the two-tailed 5% critical values. Is it inside or outside them?
steps.title: Compare with the critical value and conclude

lines.text: At the 5% level (two-tailed) the critical values are $\pm \hl{4}{1.96}$.
$\hl{1}{z}$ is outside $-\hl{4}{1.96} \le \hl{1}{z} \le \hl{4}{1.96}$, so reject $H_0$. There is evidence that the mean weight of carry-on luggage has changed.

problems.final: \text{Reject } H_0\text{: the mean weight of carry-on luggage has changed}

problems.note: The result flips: z = -1.71 lies inside ±1.96, so H₀ is not rejected. The steps are the same, but the formula uses the sample standard deviation s in place of σ.

steps.ask: The supermarket claims a mean spend of €94. What are H₀ and H₁ if the test looks for a change in either direction?
steps.title: State the hypotheses

lines.text: The null hypothesis $H_0$: the mean spend is $\text{€}\hl{2}{94}$ (the supermarket is right).
The alternative hypothesis $H_1$: the mean spend is not $\text{€}\hl{2}{94}$.

steps.ask: Standardise the sample mean against the claimed mean of €94. Which mean goes on top, and what goes on the bottom?
steps.title: Calculate the test statistic

lines.text: Use $\hl{1}{z} = \dfrac{\hl{3}{\bar{x}} - \hl{2}{\mu}}{s / \sqrt{n}}$.

steps.ask: Where does z sit compared with the two-tailed 5% critical values?
steps.title: Compare with the 5% critical values

lines.text: At the 5% level (two-tailed) the critical values are $\pm \hl{4}{1.96}$.

steps.ask: Does z fall inside the critical values? What does that mean for the claim of €94?
steps.title: Conclude

lines.text: $\hl{1}{z}$ lies between $-\hl{4}{1.96}$ and $\hl{4}{1.96}$, so we do not reject $H_0$. There is not enough evidence to reject $H_0$ (the claim of $\text{€}\hl{2}{94}$).

problems.final: \text{Do not reject } H_0\ (\hl{1}{z = -1.71}).\ \text{There is not enough evidence to reject } H_0 \text{ (the claim of } \text{€}\hl{2}{94}\text{).}

problems.note: z is large and positive (the sample mean 22.16 is well above 20.79), so H₀ is rejected, as in problem 1. The steps and two-tailed test are the same as problem 2, with n = 500 and a standard deviation of 8.12.

steps.ask: What are H₀ and H₁ for a change in either direction from the 2019 mean of 20.79?
steps.title: State the hypotheses

lines.text: We test whether the mean differs from the 2019 figure in either direction, so the test is two-tailed.
Null hypothesis: the mean monthly spend has not changed.
Alternative hypothesis: the mean monthly spend has changed.

steps.ask: Which quantity is the standard error here, and how does it enter the z formula?
steps.title: Calculate the test statistic

lines.text: Use $\hl{1}{z} = \dfrac{\hl{3}{\bar{x}} - \hl{2}{\mu}}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}}$ with $\bar{x} = \hl{3}{22.16}$, $\sigma = 8.12$ (the sample standard deviation) and $n = 500$.

steps.ask: Compare the z-score with the two-tailed 5% critical values. Is it inside or outside?
steps.title: Compare with the critical value

lines.text: At the 5% level, two-tailed, the critical values are $\pm \hl{4}{1.96}$.

steps.ask: What is the decision, and how does z compare with the critical value?
steps.title: State the conclusion and reason

lines.text: Conclusion: reject $H_0$. The mean monthly spend has changed.
Reason: $\hl{1}{z = 3.7726}$ lies outside $-\hl{4}{1.96} \le \hl{1}{z} \le \hl{4}{1.96}$, so the result is significant at the 5% level.

problems.final: \text{Reject } H_0\text{: the mean monthly spend has changed, since } \hl{1}{3.7726} > \hl{4}{1.96}
